title: Meta Reveals Hardware Strategy to Investors
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc walks through Meta's hardware strategy in a news-and-analysis update with no explicit buy or sell call and no valuation — the call is recorded as UNCERTAIN. The strategy he describes is to sell AI glasses close to cost, around $500, and monetise them through a Meta Muse subscription at about $9.99 a month, which he estimates could carry roughly 70% gross margins as recurring revenue; wearables are an open category with no dominant player, unlike phones against Apple. He says he likes the evidence that the spending is working: Meta AI engagement per person has more than doubled since April, and the Muse personal agent passed 10 million downloads in about six weeks. On the financial side, he thinks Reality Labs losses have peaked and should improve as spending shifts from virtual reality to AI, puts 2026 capital spending at at least $135 billion on revised estimates, and expects 2027 capex to rise further to $150–175 billion — spending investors will only accept if the engagement and revenue evidence keeps coming. No price or DCF figure is stated in this video.
